Brian Judd

Independent candidate for Governor, Vermont · Challenger

U.S. Navy veteran and former SAG-AFTRA actor. No current occupation was found in the sources.

Brian Judd is from Barre City, where his family ran the Hooker & Whitcomb Funeral Home for more than 100 years, and he served in the U.S. Navy from 1978 to 1983. He ran for Barre City Council in 2021 and for state representative in 2022 and lost both races. He is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for governor as an independent.

Where Judd stands

Property taxes
Says he would work with the Legislature, and with the courts when necessary, to stop tax increases, lower existing taxes and return taxpayer money to Vermonters.
Affordability and cost of living (housing)
Proposes using executive orders to seek full repeal of Act 181, Vermont's 2024 land-use law. Also proposes declaring a state of emergency over homelessness and restoring loitering and vagrancy laws.
Health care
Proposes restoring state psychiatric hospitals. Argues that the current 22-bed facility in Berlin is not a true psychiatric hospital.
State workforce
Proposes broad audits of state government and of Vermont nonprofit organizations.
Climate and energy
Opposes Vermont's climate spending. Argues that Vermont produces about 0.02% of global emissions and that state climate programs raise electric costs without changing global temperatures.

Background

  • U.S. Navy, October 1978 to December 1983 (honorable discharge)
  • SAG-AFTRA member for almost 30 years
  • Graduated from Spaulding High School in Barre, 1978
  • Lived in California for about 25 years and returned to Barre in 2019
  • Ran unsuccessfully for Barre City Council, 2021
  • Ran unsuccessfully for state representative from Barre City, 2022
  • Has not held elected office

Also running for Governor

  • June Goodband Peace and Justice
  • Amanda Janoo Democratic/Progressive
  • Dean Roy Freedom and Unity
  • Phil Scott Republican
